title: Opinion: Why Nvidia's stock is dodging the AI credit scare that is crushing Broadcom and Oracle
source_used: International Business Times Singapore, relaying MarketWatch's 10 Oct 2026 analysis (MarketWatch page blocked, HTTP 401); Crypto Briefing read for the credit-default-swap figures
key_facts: MarketWatch reported on 10 Oct that Oracle shares had fallen more than 40% since 2 June and Broadcom about 25%.
Nvidia's forward earnings estimates had risen more than 30%, against gains of more than 20% for Broadcom and about 14% for Oracle, which helped cushion its valuation decline.
MarketWatch's analysis found rising forward earnings estimates helped offset Nvidia's contracting price-to-earnings multiple and widening credit-default-swap spreads.

Separate coverage put Oracle's credit default swap spread at a record 261 basis points and Nvidia's at around 80 to 87; wider spreads mean investors demand more compensation for credit risk, not that a default is imminent.
Oracle's free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion for fiscal 2026 and it reported $638 billion in contracted future revenue; Broadcom's top five customers were about 55% of net revenue.
Nvidia has committed nearly $50 billion to frontier AI labs, so a slowdown among major customers could still affect it.
quote_evidence: MarketWatch reported on Oct. 10 that Oracle shares had fallen more than 40% since June 2, while Broadcom was down about 25%.
Wider CDS spreads mean investors demand more compensation for credit risk; they do not mean a default is imminent.
Wider spreads signal rising financing concerns, not proof that the AI boom is ending.
why_it_matters_hint: Credit worries about AI spending are hitting heavily indebted AI builders harder than Nvidia, whose earnings forecasts keep rising.
notes: MarketWatch original is an opinion column and is blocked; the text read is a second-hand account that names MarketWatch's findings, so the source is MarketWatch as relayed by IBT Singapore. The CDS record figures (Oracle 261, Broadcom 136, Nvidia 80 to 87 basis points) are consistent with Crypto Briefing's separate report and with Bloomberg-based coverage in our 9 Oct 2026 edition.
